requirements.requirement: Serve working HTTPS on node1 TCP port 8443.
requirements.summary: nginx was active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443. Trusted requests returned the expected response before and after restart, and the final served certificate was directly observed.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before it expires.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active, persistent timer schedules renewal checks. When a one-day certificate was placed inside the seven-day renewal window, the normal systemd renewal service replaced it with a new 30-day certificate and reported success; the final threshold check correctly made no further change.

requirements.requirement: Have the HTTPS service load each renewed certificate while continuing to answer requests.
requirements.summary: Both forced and threshold-driven renewal tests changed the certificate serial served by nginx, preserved its master PID through graceful reload, completed 100 concurrent HTTPS requests with zero failures, and returned a successful post-rotation response.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: HTTPS works on port 8443, a due certificate is automatically renewed before expiry, nginx loads the renewed certificate without observed request failures, and the finished configuration survives the mandatory node restart. Minor hygiene issues remain: an unnecessary port-80 listener and three abandoned /tmp artifacts.
limitations: Continuity was tested with two bounded 100-request probes rather than prolonged production traffic.
The renewal schedule and due-window behavior were directly tested, but the evidence does not span the certificate's real multi-week lifetime.
The lifecycle snapshot shows nginx listening on port 80, but available evidence does not establish whether firewalld made that port externally reachable.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was healthy after completion: no failed services or package inconsistency were observed. The required restart protocol was complete and independently corroborated by the lifecycle boot IDs; pre-restart HTTPS, certificate, nginx, and timer health were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and service/certificate/timer/firewall state recovered. Hygiene deductions are for retained, unnecessary state: enabling the packaged default nginx configuration also left nginx listening on port 80, although only 8443 was required (cmd-6f538a33da32425d; retained; external reachability of port 80 was not established). Three evidence/install artifacts were also abandoned in /tmp: nginx-install.log from cmd-95ecf09710df46e4, https-rotation-probe from cmd-c3ce9df0e3704c7b, and https-threshold-probe from cmd-c47281670bd04bc5. The temporary near-expiry certificate mutation itself was bounded and restored through the demonstrated renewal path, so it is not treated as unnecessary.
